confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'This confirms that the mechanical thermostat inside the cavity is failing and losing its calibration' / 'the issue is almost certainly a failing mechanical thermostat'

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'Please call an engineer to replace the thermostat' plus panel 'To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number' with no temperature measurement taken

rationale: The assistant handled the messy opener well, asked a sensible knobs-vs-display question and correctly proposed the oven-thermometer test, keeping all advice safe and referring thermostat replacement to an engineer. However, once the customer had no thermometer it treated the ambiguous neon behaviour ('sometimes goes off after about 10 mins') as confirming a failing thermostat, declared it 'almost certainly' the fault and pushed a replacement-part panel, when the ground truth is genuinely uncertain and a flattened seal, wobbly knob and inconsistent preheating were never explored. It also repeated the same heading, explanation and model-number panel after the customer said she could not find the label. The engineer referral is an acceptable landing point, but the confidence and part focus are unsupported by the evidence.
